record.title: Lebombo closure during Mozambique election unrest
record.direction: Both directions affected, with selective homeward returns to each country; exact chronology differs by side and category.
record.movement: Travellers and freight, with intermittent homeward movements and selective truck releases
record.exceptions: Homebound Mozambican nationals admitted during November6/7 temporary opening; perishable/fuel trucks reportedly released; later homebound people, empty return trucks and recovery vehicles. Timing and exact category bounds remain incomplete.
record.enforcement: Primary BMA closure notice and dated South African reporting establish closure and temporary passage; Mozambican reporting supplies separately attributed side-specific reopening accounts.
record.relationship: One interrupted regime retained under stable SC05; no new duplicate phase rows. Earlier temporary openings, November7 reclosure and November8/9 restoration milestones recorded explicitly; later recurrence SC26 remains separate.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; current status not inferred
record.official_rationale: Public safety after vehicles were burned on the Mozambican side
record.context: Post-election unrest produced repeated interruption and partial passage at Lebombo/Ressano Garcia. The November5 closure was interrupted before the previously recorded November8 partial opening; cargo/full-restoration accounts follow November9.
record.uncertainty: SABC quotes a Wednesday November6 partial reopening lasting overnight; EWN describes Thursday November7 morning opening before renewed closure. Rádio Moçambique on November8 attributes homeward opening on its side to November7 afternoon. These may describe different side/category phases; timing is unresolved. November8 is not the first relaxation. No continuous November5–8 closure retained. Later recurrence remains SC26.

historical.duration_note: No exact continuous interval. Temporary homebound passage before November8 and renewed closure invalidate the former November5–8 three-day spell. November8 retained solely as a later partial-opening milestone.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Primary BMA closure and EWN reporting confirm repeated suspension.
